%1$s will be removed from the app together with its saved passwords and keys. Nothing changes on the server itself.

First connection to %1$s. Compare this fingerprint with the server\'s host key, for example by running ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub in your provider\'s web console. Trust it only if they match.
The key presented by %1$s does not match the saved one. This is expected after reinstalling the OS, but it can also mean the connection is being intercepted.
3x-ui has not been deployed by this app yet. One-click deploy installs the official release %1$s, sets a random panel port, path, login and password, and creates a VLESS + Reality inbound.

Installs 3x-ui %1$s with the official script, gets a Let\'s Encrypt certificate for the server\'s address (port 80 must be reachable), opens ports in the firewall, sets a random panel port, path, login and password, generates Reality keys with xray x25519 and creates an inbound on port 443 (or a free port if 443 is taken).
Automatic: best one from the list
Version on the server: %1$s. What should happen to it?
Inbounds and clients stay. Login, password, panel port and path are replaced with new random ones.
The current database is backed up to /root/xui-backup on the server, then 3x-ui starts from scratch.
You can leave this screen: the deployment keeps running in the background and is shown in a notification.
A deployment started earlier is not being monitored. The server may still be working on it.
Subscriptions on this panel are served over plain HTTP. Links work, but their content travels unencrypted; set the subscription certificate in the panel\'s settings to fix this.
The Reality target could not be verified from the server. If clients can\'t connect, redeploy with another target.

Unique name in the panel, e.g. phone-anna
Scan the QR code in a client app (v2rayNG, Hiddify, Streisand, Happ…) or share the link.

Installs 3x-ui %1$s the same way, with a Let\'s Encrypt certificate, then creates the inbound you describe below. VLESS and Trojan always use Reality; combinations that would send credentials unencrypted or that Xray does not support are not offered.
no TLS, the protocol encrypts traffic itself
Must be free on the server; deployment stops if it is taken.
A site that serves TLS 1.3 with HTTP/2; pick one or type your own.

Keeps the installed version, port, path, inbounds, clients and subscription settings. The login and password are replaced so the app can sign in; if the panel has no valid public certificate, a Let\'s Encrypt one is issued. No inbound is created.
Connected clients will be dropped for a few seconds and reconnect on their own.
On 3x-ui 2.x a client stays in the inbound it was created in.
%1$s will be removed from all inbounds together with its traffic statistics. Its subscription link stops working.
Used traffic of %1$s is set to zero. If the client was disabled for exceeding its limit, it is enabled again.
Counted from the first connection; changing it sets a fixed date.
Port must be between 1 and 65535 and differ from the SSH port.
Enter a host name, for example www.microsoft.com.
This transport is not available for the chosen protocol.
Automatic sign-in failed: %1$s Sign in manually below.
The panel\'s TLS certificate is not trusted (expired, issued for another address, or not from a public authority). The connection was refused.
Port 80 is already in use on the server. Let\'s Encrypt needs it to issue the panel certificate; free it and deploy again.
A Let\'s Encrypt certificate needs a public IPv4 address or a domain name. Add the server by its IPv4 address or domain.
Let\'s Encrypt could not issue a certificate for this server. Port 80 must be reachable from the internet (check the provider\'s firewall too). See the log for details.
Connect your VPS over SSH. The app installs and manages the 3x-ui panel on it.
Its A record must point at the server\'s IP, with Cloudflare proxying off. With a domain the panel gets a Let\'s Encrypt certificate for it and self-steal becomes available.
Enter a domain name like vpn.example.com, without http:// or a path.
%1$s does not resolve yet. Create an A record pointing at %2$s and try again in a few minutes.
%1$s points at %2$s, not at this server (%3$s). Fix the A record (and turn off Cloudflare proxying), then try again: Let\'s Encrypt cannot issue a certificate otherwise.
The password is not stored in the app. Redeploy or take over the panel to set a new one.
Which browser\'s TLS handshake clients imitate. chrome suits most cases.
Could not download Caddy for the self-steal site. The server needs access to github.com.
The downloaded Caddy archive did not match its pinned checksum and was discarded.
The self-steal site could not be set up. See the log for details.
Self-steal needs a domain. Add one in the server settings.
No inbounds yet. Add one to let clients connect.
Inbound updated, Xray restarted. Clients need to refresh their subscription.
%1$s will be deleted together with its %2$d client(s) and their traffic statistics. This cannot be undone.
Disguised as a website on your own domain, served from this server with a real certificate.
Keys, short IDs and clients stay the same. Clients need to refresh their subscription afterwards.
Suitable: TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, %1$d ms from the server
Not suitable as a Reality target from this server

The server gets a small website for %1$s with a Let’s Encrypt certificate (Caddy, reachable only from the server itself). Reality forwards everything that is not your client to it, so anyone probing the server sees an ordinary site.
Move %1$s onto it (%2$d client(s) keep working after a subscription refresh)
Could not update the site page
This file does not fit: a single HTML file in UTF-8, up to 1 MB, is needed.
Your page is a single self-contained index.html: styles and images must be embedded in the file.
The page %1$s shows to anyone who opens it. Without a file of your own, a new random template is put there.
Open your domain in a browser: you should see the decoy site. Clients need to refresh their subscription.
No inbound uses the self-steal site any more. Remove Caddy and the site from the server?
Reality disguises traffic as a website on %1$s that this server serves itself (Caddy with the same Let’s Encrypt certificate). Recommended when you have a domain.
Reality disguises traffic as a well-known site such as www.microsoft.com.
The RoscomVPN geo files could not be downloaded or did not match their published checksum. The server needs access to github.com.
The subscription gives Happ and INCY the RoscomVPN routing profile: Russian and Belarusian services go direct, everything else through the VPN.
Routing profiles in the subscription need 3x-ui v3. Update the panel to use them.

Happ and INCY take the profile from the subscription and decide on the device what goes through the VPN. The rules and the RoscomVPN geo files update by themselves. Clients need to refresh the subscription once. Other apps (v2rayNG, Streisand…) ignore it.
The panel has a routing profile set by hand. Choosing one below replaces it.
RU/BY sites, banks, VK and Yandex direct; YouTube, Telegram, GitHub and everything else through the VPN; ads and Windows telemetry blocked.
Direct only for services and addresses on Russia’s whitelists; everything else through the VPN.
Saved. Refresh the subscription in the client.

Xray on the server refuses Russian sites and addresses (RoscomVPN geo files next to Xray, refreshed weekly). Russian services never see the server’s address, even from clients without routing; on those clients such sites stop opening through the VPN.

The app downloads the RoscomVPN geo files to the server over SSH, checks their checksums and adds two rules to the Xray template. Clients without routing (or with routing off) will not open Russian sites through the VPN.
Russian destinations are blocked on the server
Could not change the server rules
Rules and geo files: github.com/hydraponique/roscomvpn-routing, roscomvpn-geoip, roscomvpn-geosite.
Every protocol, transport and security option of the panel, as in its own inbound form.
No nodes yet. A node is another server with 3x-ui that this panel manages: its inbounds are created and listed here, while clients and subscriptions stay on this panel. Tap + to add one.
The app installs 3x-ui on the server the same way as here (Let\'s Encrypt certificate, API token) and registers it as a node.
The panel is already running: enter its address, port, path and API token (x-ui setting -getApiToken on the node).
The node is registered on the panel
The node is removed from the panel
3x-ui is installed, but the main panel has not accepted the node yet. Register it again once the server is reachable.
3x-ui is not installed on this server yet.
%1$s will be removed from the panel. Its inbounds are not moved anywhere, and 3x-ui keeps running on the node itself.
The app forgets %1$s and its credentials. Nothing is changed on the server.
Connect a 3x-ui panel that is already running. The main panel probes it before saving.
Host name or IP of the node\'s panel
Created on the node: x-ui setting -getApiToken
Leave empty to keep the stored token
For nodes on a LAN or 10.x / 192.168.x addresses
Plain HTTP: the token and traffic stats go unencrypted.
Anyone between the panels can impersonate the node and read its API token.
The main panel presents its client certificate instead of a token. Paste the main panel\'s CA into the node\'s trust settings first (in the web panel).
Fetch it from the node, then compare it with the node\'s certificate
An outbound of the main panel\'s Xray to connect to the node through.
Load the node\'s inbounds to pick them.
SSH access to the server that becomes a node. The app installs 3x-ui there and registers it on the main panel. Its inbounds are then managed from the main panel.
This server is a node: its inbounds, clients and subscriptions are managed from the main panel.
This server is meant to be a node but is not registered on the main panel yet. Register it from the main panel\'s node list.
%1$s is removed from the app and, if the main panel can be reached, from its nodes. 3x-ui keeps running on the server.
3x-ui is installed, but the main panel did not accept the node. Open the node list and tap Register once the server is reachable from the main panel.
3x-ui %1$s is out. It will be installed on:
Settings, inbounds and clients are kept. VPN connections drop for about a minute while each panel restarts.
Can\'t be updated from the app
XUI Manager %1$s is out (you have %2$s). Download the APK from the release page and install it over this one; servers and settings are kept.
Xray %1$s is out (the server runs %2$s). The panel downloads it from GitHub and restarts Xray; VPN connections drop for about a minute.
The Xray update did not finish
GitHub did not return the release: %1$s

Runs apt update and apt upgrade (dnf upgrade on RHEL-like systems) on %1$s. This can take several minutes. If the update needs a restart, the server reboots automatically and VPN connections drop for 1–2 minutes.
The system is up to date
The system is updated. The server reboots in a minute and is back 1–2 minutes later.
The package manager reported an error. See the log for details.
Another package manager (often automatic security updates) is busy on the server. Try again in a few minutes.
Packages are updated, but the restart could not be scheduled. Restart the server manually.
